question.text: The volume (in ml) of 0.1 M  <math><mtext>AgN</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>O</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math>  required for complete precipitation of chloride ions present in 30 mL of 0.01 M solution of  <math><mo>[</mo><mtext>Cr</mtext><mfenced close="]" separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><msub><mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><mtext>Cl</mtext></mrow></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mtext>C</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>l</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> , as silver chloride is close to

solution.text:
Number of ionisable Cl- in [CrH2O)5ClCl2 is 2

Millimoles of Cl-=30×0.01×2=0.6

Millimoles of Ag+ required =0.6

0.6=0.1 V

V=6 ml
